newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Manager says Air Zimbabwe viability under threat.
newsitem.headline: Manager says Air Zimbabwe viability under threat.

text.p: Zimbabwe's state-owned airline, where some 70 pilots went on strike on Friday for higher pay, can be viable only if run on a totally commercial basis, the company's chief executive said.

Air Zimbabwe Corporation acting managing director Peter Chikumba said in a report published on Friday that the airline's profit had declined to an estimated Z$10 million (U.S.$896,000) in the financial year ended June 1996 from Z$31.3 million the previous year.
"From a purely financial point of view and the experience of the corporation, Air Zimbabwe needs a minimum of Z$20 million profit to cover any unforeseen events," he said.
He said increased competition and old aircraft expensive to run had contributed to Air Zimbabwe's problems, although non-core business operations such as ground-handling were profitable.
"Increased competition on the regional and international sectors contributed to the erosion of the revenue base as less passengers were carried compared to the previous year," Mukumba said.
"To generate revenue and keep the airline going it is recommended that government urgently approve the commercialisation strategy in total and action the enabling Act of Parliament," Mukumba said.
He said the airline had to cut high running costs and terminate unprofitable routes.

"The profitability of the corporation is on the decline and its existence cannot be guaranteed if some of the mentioned recommendations are not implemented as a matter of urgency. The business of our business is the bottom line," he said in the report published by the weekly Zimbabwe Independent newspaper.
